how_to_run: Scenarios: one subagent runs the skill, a second subagent plays the person from 'persona' and never reveals more than asked. If the skill-running agent cannot start the checker itself, the coordinator starts it strictly by references/verifier.md and the run report says so. A third, fresh subagent judges the finished interview-log.md and brief.md against 'checks' and the persona's hidden truth. Triggers: give each query to a model with this skill installed among others and record whether it loads the skill.

should: help me explain what I want from a new website, I can't put it into words
I have this CRM mechanic in my head but I can't describe it to my boss
interview me and write up what I actually want
Помоги сформулировать, чего я хочу от нового процесса, у меня всё в голове
Ich habe eine Idee, kann sie aber nicht erklären. Frag mich aus und schreib es auf.
should_not: build me a landing page for my bakery
write the email sequence for our onboarding campaign
grill me on this migration plan before I ship it

scenarios.opening: I want a website for my practice but honestly I don't know what should be on it.
scenarios.persona: Independent family therapist, 8 years in practice, gets clients by word of mouth. Wants fewer 'is this for me?' calls and more people booking a first session ready. Has no idea about pages or positioning; answers 'I don't know' to structure questions. Firmly: no prices on the site, no blog. Undecided: whether to show her photo. Will accept one suggestion about a short 'who I work with' section and reject a suggestion about online booking.
checks: Questions arrive one per message
Mode choice is offered before the first question and logged
Every suggestion is logged as 'suggestion' and marked as such in the chat
The rejected online-booking suggestion is absent from the brief
The accepted 'who I work with' idea is in the brief
'No prices, no blog' appear as out of scope
The photo question is an open question, not a decision
The checker subagent ran on the draft before it was shown; the log holds the shown brief as a `draft` entry headed by that verdict
Every option message offers two or three options
Any change to the brief after it was shown went through the checker and was shown to the person again; the final brief.md is the text the person last confirmed
The checker's OPEN IN LOG list includes the photo entry and places it in open questions
The brief lets the studio estimate the work: each thing they would need to ask before quoting is either answered or listed as an open question

scenarios.opening: Хочу описать механику реактивации для руководителя, она у меня в голове, но словами не получается
scenarios.persona: CRM-маркетолог туроператора. Механика: клиенты, не покупавшие 12+ месяцев, получают письмо с подборкой по прошлому направлению, через 3 дня без открытия — SMS, после клика без покупки — звонок менеджера в течение суток. Цель — вернуть 5% спящей базы за квартал. Читатель — руководитель отдела, должен одобрить бюджет на SMS. Не знает точной стоимости SMS — это открытый вопрос. Отвечает короткими фразами с опечатками.
checks: The whole conversation and the brief are in Russian
The interviewer offers no ideas of its own (mode A): no examples, answer choices or formulas inside questions
The log keeps the persona's typos verbatim
The brief names the reader (head of department) and the action (approve SMS budget)
12 months, 3 days, 24 hours and 5% per quarter appear exactly as given
SMS cost is listed as an open question with no invented figure
No implementation (templates, segments in a tool, code) is produced
Questions arrive one per message
The brief does not present the manager's call as the step after the SMS: it follows a click without purchase
'In one sentence' states the mechanic itself, not what the document is

scenarios.mode_the_persona_picks: A, then switches to B midway
scenarios.persona: Owner of a 15-person agency. Wants a written process for how a new client request goes from first email to a signed estimate, for the team wiki. Knows the steps vaguely: someone replies within a day, a call, an estimate, owner signs off on anything over 10,000. Not sure who should own the first reply; after switching to mode B accepts the suggestion that the account manager on duty owns it. Changes his mind once: first says estimates go out in 2 days, later says 3.
checks: With no opening message the interviewer starts the log before saying anything, logs the mode explanation as a 'question', and asks for the mode first
The mode switch is logged as a 'mode' entry holding the person's own words, not the interviewer's summary
The brief uses 3 days (the later answer), not 2
The 10,000 sign-off threshold is kept exactly
The first-reply owner appears only because the persona accepted the suggestion, and the log shows that acceptance
The brief is written for the team (readers who follow it), not for the owner
Questions arrive one per message
Every message after the person's first reply is in the language the person writes in
Any change to the brief after the person confirmed it was shown to them again before finishing
The team can follow the brief without coming back: who does each step and when is stated or listed as an open question
'In one sentence' states the process itself, not what the page is
No statement in the brief rests only on a `draft` entry confirmed by a general "yes"
